title: The grey light blocks in caves
question: Is the light coming off the crystals now the right shape? And does the faint blocking further out from the big halo still bother you?
context_md:
This is the thing you picked out twice without being asked — "very large
uniform gray blocks with blurry light coming off it", and on a different
card, "the problem is the big sharp squares that look like giant white
gray pixels".

Same cave, same seed, same camera. Only the glow term differs.

It was not a smoothing problem. The light field stores one value per 8x8
cells, and — worse — it quantises the *emitter* to that grid before any
diffusion runs: a two-cell crystal becomes a filled 8x8 square first, then
gets smeared over about sixteen cells, aligned to the field's lattice
instead of to the crystal. Smoothing that harder just gives a vaguer
sixteen-cell blob, which is why the older note in the bug file ("halo
block-edge softening, low priority") was aimed at the wrong thing.

The fix gives each glowing *cell* its own short-range falloff and leaves
the coarse field to carry the far tail. It is gated so it can only sharpen
light that is already there — otherwise a crystal would shine through a
wall.

Costs nothing per frame on a settled world: the splat is rebuilt only when
a cell in a glowing chunk actually changes. Worst frame across the ascii
scenes is unchanged at 0.33-2.15 ms.

It is a selector — `'` in the app, and the status line names it when you
switch back. I have defaulted it to the new one rather than leaving it to
you, because you had already called the old one bad twice; say the word if
you would rather it were the other way.

One thing I did **not** chase, and you can see it: further out from a big
halo the coarse field's blocks are still faintly there. Growing the radius
until they leave the screen would cost the whole point of a short-range
term. Tell me if it still reads wrong at that distance.
